items.title: Who Will Fill the Pulpits? Ligon Duncan, Tom Gibbs, and Derek Radney on the coming pastoral shortage
items.description:
The PCA is approaching an important long-term question: How will the denomination raise up enough qualified pastors to serve its churches, plant new ones, and lead growing ministries in the decades ahead? A large generation of pastors is nearing retirement, the PCA continues to grow, and RUF and other ministries are expanding into new places. At the same time, fewer young men are imagining pastoral ministry as a possible vocation, financial barriers can make seminary difficult to pursue, and pastors are leaving pulpits because of burnout, early retirement, and other pressures.

These converging factors raise questions about the entire pastoral pipeline—from identifying and encouraging potential ministers to training, supporting, and placing them well. That work cannot belong to seminaries alone. It requires local churches, presbyteries, campus ministries, seminaries, and the wider denomination to see themselves as partners in raising up the next generation.

In this conversation, Derek Radney speaks with seminary presidents Ligon Duncan and Tom Gibbs about the challenges and opportunities ahead—and how the whole church can work together to prepare pastors for a lifetime of faithful ministry.

items.title: The Long Road to BCO 34-1: An Interview with Mel Duncan, Howie Donahoe, and Derek Radney
items.description:
In this conversation, former PCA General Assembly Moderators Howie Donahoe and Mel Duncan join Derek Radney to discuss the proposed revision to BCO 34-1 and the doctrine of assumption of original jurisdiction.

Drawing on decades of experience in the PCA's judicial process, they trace the history of BCO 34-1, explain why previous attempts to revise it fell short, and walk through how the current proposal seeks to provide a clearer, more workable process while preserving the Presbyterian principle of respecting lower courts.

items.title: After the General Assembly: Reflections on Trust, Unity, and the Work Ahead
items.author_or_contributor_as_printed: Derek Radney, Geoff Ziegler, Erik Bonkovsky
items.description:
The 53rd PCA General Assembly brought record numbers of overtures, voting delays, and several significant decisions—but it also revealed something more encouraging. In this conversation, Derek Radney, Geoff Ziegler, and Eric Bonkovsky reflect on why the Assembly ultimately fostered confidence rather than anxiety, how face-to-face statesmanship prevailed over online controversy, what the Assembly's decisions say about the health of the PCA, and the important conversations that still lie ahead.

items.title: What Kind of Church Are We Becoming? A Conversation with David Richter and Derek Radney
items.description: In this interview, Derek Radney speaks with Rev. David Richter, co-chair of the board of the Alliance for Mission and Renewal, about the AMR board’s recent statement and the season facing the PCA. Drawing from a year of listening across the denomination, the conversation addresses concerns about tone, trust, and trajectory, and introduces a vision for renewal rooted in a “confessional-missional center.” This is not a call to shift doctrine, but to recover a deeper stability—marked by theological seriousness, humility, and renewed focus on the church’s shared mission.

items.title: Three Questions with Casey Cockrum
items.description:
In this installment of the AMR Three Questions Series, Christine Gordon sits down with Casey Cockrum, Assistant Vice President of the Campus Staff Department with Reformed University Fellowship (RUF).

Casey shares about her work helping recruit, develop, and care for the women who serve as campus staff across RUF ministries. She also tells a powerful story about prayer, perseverance, and the launch of an RUF ministry at Wellesley College after a decade of prayer.

In this conversation, Casey reflects on:
• Her role serving and supporting RUF campus staff
• How God is working through campus ministry across the country
• What encouragement and support look like for those serving on college campuses

The Three Questions Series highlights leaders across the PCA and ministries connected to the Alliance for Mission and Renewal, giving them space to share their work, stories of God’s faithfulness, and ways the broader church can come alongside them.

Learn more about AMR:
https://a4mr.org

Learn more about RUF:
https://ruf.org

items.title: Three Questions Series: Kathy Clow of Mission to the World
items.description:
In this installment of AMR’s Three Questions series, Chris Gordon sits down with Kathy Clow, whose work quietly spans continents, callings, and seasons of life. Kathy and her husband John have served with Mission to the World for nearly twenty-five years, most recently in Central America, where Kathy has long been involved in missionary care and encouragement.

In the conversation, Kathy reflects on life and ministry shaped by long obedience, the formation that comes through counseling work, and what it means to care well for marriages, families, and women serving faithfully across the global church.

items.title: The Founding Vision of the PCA: Derek Radney and Sean Michael Lucas
items.description:
In a time of growing polarization within the PCA, questions about our identity have taken on new urgency. In this conversation with Derek Radney, historian and pastor Sean Michael Lucas revisits the denomination’s founding vision and considers how a clearer grasp of our history can inform the church’s life today.

Together, they explore competing narratives about the PCA’s origins, examine key moments and debates from its early years, and reflect on what the historical record reveals about who the PCA has been from the beginning. As Radney guides the conversation, they consider how historical clarity might help the church navigate disagreement with greater faithfulness, patience, and purpose.

items.title: Urban vs  Suburban Ministry: An AMR Conversation
items.description:
Conversations about urban and suburban ministry often collapse into stereotypes or strategies. This conversation slows things down, asking deeper questions about how place forms us, unique challenges and opportunities of the urban and suburban contexts, and what faithfulness looks like across different contexts. 

Listen to these seven seasoned pastors dig into the way context shapes the church’s instincts, priorities, and blind spots—and what a more honest, attentive posture toward place might require for genuine mission and renewal.

In this episode of the Three Question Series from the Alliance for Mission and Renewal, Christine Gordon talks with Denine Blevins, Executive Director of Parakaleo, about caring well for the women who serve in church-planting contexts.

Denine shares practical wisdom and heartfelt encouragement for pastors, planters, and leaders who want to build healthier, more sustainable ministries—ones that nurture the spiritual and emotional wellbeing of everyone involved.

items.title: The Sage and the Sermon: The Five Moods of Preaching with Zack Eswine
items.description: Preaching in a fractured world requires more than clarity—it requires wisdom. In this conversation, pastor and author Zack Eswine, draws on his years at Riverside Church and teaching at Covenant Seminary to explore how preachers can move beyond “what is true and what to do” into a richer range of moods—questions, imaginings, longings, and hopes—that mirror the wisdom and gentleness of Jesus.

items.title: Reaching Our Culture Through Presiding and Preaching
items.description:
Many churches emphasize either reaching the lost or growing the saved, but few churches do both well. In this seminar, pastor Aaron Chung (Exilic Church, NYC) walks us through ways even the ordinary rhythms of church can be extraordinary means of outreach, shaping the minds and hearts of congregations in a weekly rhythm of discipleship. Both preaching and presiding (the things that happen during a service outside of the sermon) can become more than internal acts of discipleship, but also missional practices that help the church reach its surrounding culture.

If your congregation wrestles with the balance between “growing the saved” and “reaching the lost,” this conversation offers encouragement, clarity, and practical next steps.
